question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨x{e}^{y},z,0⟩$ and the scalar field $f(x,y,z)=x-{e}^{y}.$ Given that

$$
∇\times F=⟨-1,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩,\,∇f=⟨1,-{e}^{y},0⟩,
$$

calculate $∇\times (f\,F)$ at the point $(2,0,-3).$
question.worked_solution:
We shall use the following identity:

$$
∇\times (f\,F)=f∇\times F+∇f\times F
$$

First, we compute $∇f\times F.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f\times F & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -{e}^{y} & 0 \\ x{e}^{y} & z & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =[-{e}^{y}(0)-0(z)]i-[1(0)-0(x{e}^{y})]j+[1(z)-(-{e}^{y})(x{e}^{y})]k \\  & =0\,i-0\,j+(z+x{e}^{2y})\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F) & =f∇\times F+∇f\times F \\  & =(x-{e}^{y})⟨-1,0,-x{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,x{e}^{2y}-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩+⟨0,0,z+x{e}^{2y}⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{y}-x,0,2x{e}^{2y}+z-{x}^{2}{e}^{y}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\times (f\,F)(2,0,-3) & =⟨{e}^{0}-2,0,2(2){e}^{2(0)}+(-3)-(2)^{2}{e}^{0}⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
